newsitem.title: UK: Blair vows "wise...not big" school spending.
newsitem.headline: Blair vows "wise...not big" school spending.

text.p: Opposition Labour leader Tony Blair on Monday promised Labour would be "wise spenders and not big spenders" on education if it won the forthcoming election.

In a major policy speech at Ruskin College, Oxford, Blair said: "With the help of proper research and dissemination on what works, it is possible to achieve a 30 percent increase in education performance within exisiting resources."
But Blair, who said education would be a priority of a Labour government, said that even within these constraints he promised growth in education.

Among pledges repeated by Blair on Monday were promises to redirect money from assisted place schemes at private schools towards primary state education to cut class sizes and a public-private partnership to renew dilapidated buildings.
Blair also said money from the national lottery should be designated to support projects for children, young people and teachers once the Millennium Fund closed in the year 2000.
Blair praised some of the reforms introduced by the ruling Conservative party, including the introduction of a national curriculum and local management of schools.

But he said the ruling party had allowed spending on education to slip as a share of national income because of its failure to deal with unemployment and inequality, and he accused the government of allowing mass underperformance in schools.

Introducing a new policy, Blair said failing local schools could come under the temporary management of headteachers from successful neighbouring schools. If introduced, a pilot scheme would begin in primary schools, he said. -- London Newsroom +44-171-542-7768
